Properties linked to money laundering case lift auction sales value in 3Q2026
article:
The auction market saw 163 listings during the third quarter of this year, including 26 linked to Singapore’s $3 billion money laundering case, according to a Knight Frank Singapore research report published on Oct 26.

In late August, Deloitte Singapore — which is handling the liquidation of non-cash assets seized in the case —  said over 80 real estate properties would be among assets auctioned in phases between September 2026 and mid-2027.

Of the 26 seized properties listed for auction in 3Q2026, four were successfully sold under the hammer.

They comprise two units at Modern Modern, a condo in River Valley, and two units at Wallich Residence , the residential component of Guoco Tower in Tanjong Pagar. Both are 99-year leasehold projects.

The Martin Modern units were both two-bedders that fetched $2.12 million and $2.08 million, while the Wallich Residence units comprised four-bedders that sold for $6.6 million and $5.48 million.

All four properties were sold below their respective opening bid prices.

Together, the properties fetched a combined sales value of $16.3 million. This accounted for  two-thirds of the auction market’s total gross sales value of $24.1 million across nine properties sold in 3Q2026.

Based on the 163 total listings in the third quarter, the nine properties sold translates to an auction success rate of 5.5%,  similar to the 5.7% rate garnered in 2Q2026.

“The high-profile listings have drawn greater attention to property auctions, but buyers remain selective,” said Nicholas Keong, Knight Frank’s head of auction, residential and private office.

Auction listings in the third quarter included 77 mortgagee sales and 41 owner's sales. The remaining 45 included the properties seized in the money laundering case as well as other auction sale types (MCST, sheriff, estate and public trustee sales).

The 77 mortgagee sale listings represent a 29.4% decline from the quarter before. They comprised 38 residences, 29 industrial properties, nine retail shops and one office unit.

Two of the residences were sold through auction: a three-bedder at Ava Towers , a freehold condo off Balestier Road in District 12, and a two-bedder at Hilltops , a freehold condo on Cairnhill Circle in District 9.

Owner listings, which rose 28.1% q-o-q from the 32 listings in 2Q2026, were largely made up of residences (30), followed by industrial (9) and retail (2) properties.

Only one owner's sale listing was sold in the third quarter: a freehold one-bedroom unit at residential development Suites @Braddell that fetched $636,600, 1.3% above its opening price.

Two properties that were auctioned successfully were MCST sales. They consisted of a three-bedroom unit at Orchid Park Condominium in Yishun and a ramp-up warehouse unit at The Westcom , a Business 2 industrial development in Tuas.

Knight Frank's Keong expects the auction market to “remain stable” through the rest of the year, supported by “a steady stream of mortgagee and owner sales”.

Despite heightened interest from the introduction of properties linked to the money laundering case, auction bidding activity and prices achieved continue to rely on buyers’ assessment of  “the fundamental values of these properties based on their individual characteristics”, he added.

title: Park Hyatt Phu Quoc to debut in December; Fusion opens Legacy Hanoi
article:
Vietnam's hospitality scene will see two more properties debuting this year — Park Hyatt is set to open its first resort in the country on Phu Quoc island in December 2026, while Fusion Hotel Group has launched its 218-room Legacy Hanoi in September.

Park Hyatt Phu Quoc

Park Hyatt Phu Quoc will occupy a 65ha site along 1.7km of white-sand beach on the island's southwest coast.

Inspired by traditional Vietnamese coastal villages, the resort is arranged around courtyards, shaded pathways and gardens leading towards the sea.

Search for the latest New Launches , to find out the transaction prices and available units

Accommodation will comprise 114 guestrooms and suites, 54 pool villas, as well as The Manor — an eight-bedroom private residence designed for multigenerational stays.

At the centre of the resort, The Courtyard will house six dining venues, two ocean-facing infinity pools and a sunset bar.

Dining options include Fisherman's, a floating restaurant where guests can select seafood from a live tank, and Pepper Grill, which draws on Phu Quoc's pepper-growing heritage.

The resort will also introduce Soma Wellbeing, Park Hyatt's first spa organised around circadian rhythms. Located beside a lotus lake, it will offer traditional Vietnamese treatments alongside recovery facilities such as infrared masks and compression therapy.

Other activities include visits to local pepper farms and fish sauce producers, fishing experiences and guided activities at the island's rice paddies. A Kids' Village will offer culinary classes, dance and craft workshops.

Park Hyatt Phu Quoc is approximately 25 minutes by car from Phu Quoc International Airport, which has direct flights from Singapore and several other Asian cities.

Legacy Hanoi

Fusion Hotel Group held the grand opening of Legacy Hanoi on Sept 16, marking its debut in Vietnam's capital.

Located in the historic Ngoc Ha ward, the property comprises 85 hotel rooms and 133 serviced apartments. Accommodation ranges from studios to one- and two-bedroom units, measuring between 37 sq m (398 sq ft) and 105 sq m (1,130 sq ft).

The hotel rooms occupy floors 14 to 18, while the serviced apartments are located on floors 9 to 13 and 19 to 21.

Hotel rooms and suites feature private balconies, floor-to-ceiling windows and vintage record players. The apartments have wooden finishes with indigo blue and terracotta accents.

The interiors draw on Hanoi's heritage, with references to the historic O Quan Chuong Gate, the Red River and the five-petal peach blossom. A suspended sculpture inspired by the Vietnamese crane, or chim hac, hangs above the reception area.

On the 24th floor, Moc Loft serves contemporary interpretations of Northern Vietnamese dishes, while 24 Social and Terrace offers an open-air rooftop bar overlooking the city.

The hotel's Yen Spa, meanwhile, offers Vietnamese massage and beauty treatments, alongside an onsen facility with hot and cold pools, a sauna, steam room and relaxation lounge.

title: SGX Next 50: Top 3 REITs to Watch This Week
article:
All three
real estate investment trusts
(REITs) reporting this week spent the past year reshaping their portfolios.
However, only some of that work has reached unitholders.
Keppel REIT
(SGX: K71U),
Starhill Global REIT
(SGX: P40U) and
Lendlease Global Commercial REIT
(SGX: JYEU) report between 28 and 30 October 2026.
Two of them went shopping for assets.
The third mostly sat tight.
Here’s the thing: a bigger portfolio does not always mean a
bigger payout
for you.

Keppel REIT: Will a bigger portfolio start paying more per unit?
Keppel REIT owns 14 prime commercial assets across Singapore, Australia, South Korea and Japan, with assets under management (AUM) of S$11.8 billion as at 30 June 2026.
Keppel REIT’s purchases lifted its first-half 2026 (1H2026) numbers.
It bought a 75% interest in Top Ryde City Shopping Centre in December 2025 and took a further one-third stake in Marina Bay Financial Centre Tower 3.
Property income rose 16.7% year on year (YoY) to S$159.3 million, while distributable income expanded 22.8% to S$129.6 million.
Unitholders did not see the benefit.
Distribution per unit (DPU) fell 4.0% YoY to S$0.0261 because an enlarged unit base diluted the gains.
In other words, the pie grew, but each slice got smaller.
The buildings themselves remain well let.
Committed portfolio occupancy stood at a healthy 96.0%, accompanied by a positive rental reversion of 12.8%, meaning new and renewed leases were signed at higher rental rates.
North Asia is the soft patch.
Attributable net property income (NPI) from the region fell 12.0%YoY, while Singapore and Australia grew 23.5% and 21.2%, respectively.
So what should you watch on 28 October?
Start with KR Ginza II.
The manager previously agreed to sell the Tokyo building for JPY 11.52 billion (28.4% above its 2022 purchase cost), with completion expected in the third quarter of 2026.
Check whether it has closed.
If the REIT pays out any gain, keep that sum separate from ordinary DPU.
On debt, aggregate leverage stood at 40.0%, with a weighted average cost of debt of 3.27% per annum.
Related articles:
4 Singapore REITs to Watch in January 2026
5 Singapore REITs with the Potential to Report Increasing Distributions
Starhill Global REIT: Can new luxury tenants restart Wisma Atria’s sales?
Starhill Global REIT, or SGREIT, owns nine predominantly retail properties across six Asia-Pacific cities, with a total portfolio valuation of around S$2.7 billion as at 30 June 2026.
SGREIT is the quiet one of the trio.
For its fiscal year ended 30 June 2026 (FY2025/2026), NPI rose 0.1% YoY to S$150.3 million, while DPU rose 0.8% to S$0.0368.
Committed portfolio occupancy improved to 97.2% from 94.6% a year earlier.
Gearing stood at 35.8%, with around 80% of debt on fixed or hedged rates.
Wisma Atria is the property to watch.
Tenant sales there fell 3.7% YoY, which the manager attributed to downtime at the Level 2 façade units ahead of new luxury tenants.
Watch whether those tenants have opened and sales have turned.
Currency is another swing factor.
A stronger ringgit and Australian dollar helped lift SGREIT’s FY2025/2026 results.
A reversal would work against the REIT.
SGREIT also did not disclose rental reversion last period, so any update would reveal its pricing power.
Related articles:
JB–Singapore RTS Link: These 3 REITs Could Ride the Benefits
5 Best Singapore REITs Income Investors Can Watch for 2H
Lendlease Global Commercial REIT: How much growth is left once PLQ Mall is in the base?
Lendlease Global Commercial REIT, or LREIT, owns Jem, 313@somerset and PLQ Mall in Singapore, plus three Grade A commercial buildings in Milan.
LREIT sold Jem’s office component and bought PLQ Mall in two tranches, completed in November 2025 and March 2026.
For the fiscal year ended 30 June 2026 (FY2026), NPI rose 2.7% YoY to S$152.7 million.
Distributable income jumped 26.0% to S$110.3 million, aided by lower interest expenses and reduced perpetual securities distributions.
Full-year DPU grew at a more modest 3.0% to S$0.037.
PLQ Mall flatters the headline numbers.
Shopper traffic grew 16.4% YoY and tenant sales rose 24.0% across LREIT’s Singapore retail portfolio.
Strip out PLQ Mall, and those increases shrink to 5.2% and 4.0%.
Those are the numbers to track.
LREIT’s committed occupancy slipped to 94.6% from 95.3% a quarter earlier.
Retail occupancy stood at 98.5%, while office occupancy lagged at 89.1%.
On a positive note, LREIT has strengthened its balance sheet.
Gearing fell to 38.9% from 42.6% a year earlier, and the cost of debt dropped to 2.75% per annum.
Watch, too, for news on the 313@somerset event space, due in the second half of 2026.
Get Smart: Follow the growth down to your units
When a REIT grows through
acquisitions
, compare its distributable income growth with its DPU growth.
The gap tells you how much of that expansion you actually own.
Keppel REIT and LREIT both opened up a wide gap in their latest reporting periods.
SGREIT’s NPI barely grew, yet its DPU still rose.
So when these three report later this week, ask each one the same question: is the growth finally reaching your units?

title: TeleChoice wins new $1.3 bil contract from U Mobile
article:
TeleChoice International has won a new contract worth up to $1.3 billion from its key customer U Mobile to provide logistics services, thereby contributing positively to its earnings from FY2027 onwards.

​The new contract, which will take place after the existing one expires next February, is confirmed for the first three years with the option to extend for another two years.

"This renewal is a strong vote of confidence in us, and we are grateful for the partnership. In just three years, the network we manage for U Mobile has grown from over 600 to more than 1,000 touchpoints across Malaysia," says Pauline Wong, president and CEO of TeleChoice.

"As U Mobile extends the nationwide reach of its ULTRA5G network, we will invest further in our people, systems and automation. We will also build on this experience to take our managed services business further across the region,” she adds.

Wong Heang Tuck, CEO of U Mobile, says this renewed agreement with TeleChoice builds on the operational capabilities the two teams have developed together.

"It will help us respond to changing demand across our sales and distribution channels as we expand our 5G network nationwide. This supports our vision of being Malaysia’s preferred mobile and digital services provider," he adds.

See also: Vodafone boosts cost-cutting target for UK to £1 bil by 2032

TeleChoice International last traded at 20 cents. It is up 16.47% year to date.

title: EQT to buy Range Resources, creating largest US gas producer
article:
(Oct 26): EQT Corp agreed to buy Range Resources Corp in an all-stock deal for about US$12.8 billion, creating what it says will be the largest and only vertically integrated US natural gas producer.

The merged company will pump more than nine billion cubic feet equivalent of daily production in Appalachia, where both companies are big operators. It will hold over 30 years of drilling inventory across nearly three million net acres. EQT expects US$325 million in annual savings within two years.

Shares of Range Resources climbed 14% in premarket trading on Monday. EQT shares were down about 4%.

Range shareholders will receive 0.987 EQT shares for each share held and will own about 27% of the combined company, according to a statement. The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.

The deal is the latest step in EQT chief executive officer Toby Rice’s push to build a US gas giant with the scale to sell directly to liquified natural gas markets and power plants. A self-styled “shalennial”, Rice took control of the company in 2019 after a proxy fight. He has turned the driller into an integrated producer, adding assets across the region and re-merging with a pipeline operator in 2024.

title: Dutch government plans to cut 25,000 jobs in AI-led overhaul
article:
(Oct 26): The Dutch government aims to cut 25,000 civil servant jobs in an AI-led efficiency drive targeting annual savings of €3.5 billion (RM16.01 billion).

The central government wants to save €900 million a year by 2027, rising to €3.5 billion from 2035. That amounts to around 25,000 jobs, spread over several years, according to a government statement on Monday. The cabinet will present plans for deploying artificial intelligence to work more productively early next year.

“We cannot keep doing what we have been doing,” State Secretary for Effective Government Eric van den Burg said. “That is why we are going to make tough choices for a central government that really works: simpler, smarter, and smaller.”

The number of government officials surged to a record 160,000 at the end of 2025, up 41% compared to 2018, despite pledges by previous cabinets to scale back headcount.

The Dutch government budget deficit of 1.8% is one of the smallest in the European Union. Yet the figure and its long-term outlook still raise concerns in the Netherlands, which has a reputation for being fiscally conservative.

The cuts won’t hit equally hard everywhere, with police and defence among exempted areas.

See also: Meta seeks up to US$95 bil in equity to fund AI spending

Ministries, inspectorates and implementing agencies will be most impacted, according to a letter Van den Burg sent to parliament. Departments there could face “significant staffing implications” of reductions of 45% or even 60%.

Van den Burg emphasised that the reductions go hand-in-hand with government ambitions to cut red tape. Its flagship programme to scrap 500 unnecessary or overly bureaucratic rules per year should make the organisation “fundamentally more simple” and lessen the need for more staff.

Promising technological developments are also paving the way for fewer external hires and a smaller administration. Various AI initiatives have already been launched in recent years across different parts of the government and the goal is to “apply AI even more broadly” to increase productivity, Van den Burg says.

See also: SK Hynix shares defy AI sell-off with help from Kioxia gains

He cited a string of non-binding motions passed by parliament calling on the cabinet to increase government productivity by 20% through AI as a reason for the cuts. He also said that the push aims to work as much as possible with Dutch and European suppliers to avoid getting dependent on non-European technology.

title: Meta seeks up to US$95 bil in equity to fund AI spending
article:
(Oct 26): Meta Platforms Inc is seeking to raise as much as US$95 billion from selling common and preferred stock, tapping investors for support in the race to lead artificial intelligence’s development.

The company is offering about US$35 billion of common and preferred stock, according to a statement Monday. It will also raise about US$60 billion in an at-the-market share sale programme, which allows companies to sell shares in the open market from time to time. The ATM will consist of its planned Class C non-voting shares.

Meta’s shares pared initial losses to trade up 1.2% at US$650 each in pre-market trading on Monday in New York. Its shares have fallen 2.7% this year through Friday’s close.

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg overhauled the company’s AI operation through an aggressive hiring push and has launched new products as well as committed hundreds of billions of dollars to build out the infrastructure needed to support the models.

The company has unveiled a personal AI agent known as Muse and an AI model called Muse Wonder that leadership say is on par with OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Anthropic PBC’s Claude in terms of tasks such as coding.

title: Audi splits logos for China as carmaker fights to revive sales
article:
(Oct 26): Audi will split its logos between its two Chinese partners as the Volkswagen AG unit tries to turnaround a protracted sales slump.

Under new agreements, China FAW Group will focus on developing Audi’s luxury combustion-engine and electric vehicle business under its traditional four-ring branding. Meanwhile, SAIC Motor Corp will focus on AUDI — all caps, no rings — with EVs tailored for the Chinese market, according to a WeChat statement Monday.

Audi has been struggling with a sales slump in China. It delivered about 618,000 vehicles in China in 2025, down 5% from a year earlier. The decline is accelerating this year, with deliveries falling about 19% to 233,000 vehicles.

The restructuring reflects the wider challenge for luxury European automakers that are facing weakening demand and mounting price pressure in China. Local carmakers such as BYD Co, Xiaomi Corp and Aito have expanded their presence in higher-priced segments, using rapid product cycles and software-led features to compete with established foreign brands.

China remains Audi’s largest single market, accounting for roughly 38% of its global deliveries last year, meaning a turnaround there is critical to its broader performance. As well as the dual-brand approach, Audi recently hired Jeff Zhang, a former executive of local automaker Chery Automobile Co, to become its China unit president.

In China, the four-ring brand’s lineup includes the A6L e-tron, Q6L e-tron and new generations of the A5L and A6L.

See also: BYD’s Korea expansion challenges Hyundai dominance on home turf

Separately, AUDI launched its first model, the E5 sportback, in 2025, followed by the E7X SUV in 2026. The partners have also established a dedicated AUDI innovation and technology centre in Shanghai to deepen cooperation across future vehicle development.

SAIC Audi can continue selling four-ring models through the end of 2027 while after-sales services for both the traditional Audi range and the AUDI marque will continue without disruption, according to the statement. The company did not disclose financial terms of the agreements or provide specific sales targets for either brand.

title: SK Hynix shares defy AI sell-off with help from Kioxia gains
article:
(Oct 26): SK Hynix Inc’s shares bucked a broad sell-off in artificial intelligence (AI)-related stocks thanks to the prospect of a hefty dividend payout related to the South Korean company’s stake in Japan’s Kioxia Holdings Corp.

The supplier of AI data-centre memory plans a special dividend of about 16 trillion won (US$12 billion or $15.46 billion) to distribute the bulk of the 20 trillion won gain it booked on its Kioxia stake in the first half of the year, the DongA Ilbo newspaper reported.

SK Hynix is considering ways to share some of the gains it’s enjoyed since AI development turbocharged chip demand and prices. It plans to outline details on returning cash to shareholders alongside earnings on Wednesday. The company is deliberating a package worth 50 trillion won to 60 trillion won that includes also a potential buy-back, the Seoul Economic Daily reported late on Monday, citing unidentified people in the industry.

Shares of SK Hynix rose as much as 3%, although they pared those gains later on Monday. Bigger rival Samsung Electronics Co fell as much as 1.9%, while Kioxia’s stock declined 3.7%.

The report coincides with attempts by chipmakers to reassure investors about their big capital expenditure plans, addressing concerns over the sustainability of an AI boom and memory-chip demand. Mounting debt among data centre operators is prompting investors to pare AI-related holdings. That’s forced cloud providers, including Australia’s Firmus Grid Ltd and Britain’s Nscale, to shelve or delay initial public offerings.

See also: Palantir’s fast-selling US$170 windbreaker shows its Korea appeal

The possibility of a dividend payout, along with SK Hynix’s decision to pull the US listing of its Solidigm unit, is providing short-term support for the stock, said Kim Namho, a fund manager at Timefolio Asset Management. But “it is not a factor that will trigger a sustained rise in the stock price”, he said.

Despite persistent scepticism over the sustainability of booming demand, memory makers Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron Technology Inc and Kioxia are ratcheting up production capacity, pointing to multiyear contracts from big tech providers such as Meta Platforms Inc and Amazon.com Inc.

In 2018, Bain Capital led a group of investors including the South Korean chipmaker in an acquisition of Toshiba Corp’s former memory operations for US$18 billion. The investment gave SK Hynix indirect exposure to the Japanese flash memory maker, whose value has surged since its Tokyo listing in 2024.

See also: Musk claims US$40 bil chips debt closed, yet talks ongoing

Bain Capital sold its entire stake in flash memory chipmaker Kioxia earlier this year, but SK Hynix did not disclose the size of its resulting one-off gain. SK Hynix continues to hold Kioxia bonds that can be converted into roughly 14% of Kioxia.

title: Soilbuild Construction wins $103 mil worth of new contracts
article:
Soilbuild Construction has secured $103 million worth of new contracts, bringing its order book to $809 million as of Aug 31.

The contracts include a construction contract for an industrial facility in the north-east and a precast supply and delivery contract for a HDB project at Bukit Merah. The former is scheduled to receive its temporary occupation permit (TOP) by 1Q2028 while the Bukit Merah project is slated to be completed by 2Q2028.

The group also clinched a “significant variation order” that will see an increase in work scope for an existing construction project. This is scheduled to be completed by 2Q2027.

Lim Han Ren, Soilbuild Construction’s executive director and group CEO says the group remains “disciplined” in its tenders, as it prioritises “opportunities that align with our capabilities and commercial objectives”.

“As we celebrate Soilbuild Construction’s 50th anniversary milestone this year, we will continue to leverage on the experience and track record that we have built up over the five decades,” he says.

Shares in Soilbuild Construction closed flat at 49 cents on Oct 26.

title: Germany’s business outlook in October unexpectedly improves for sixth month
article:
(Oct 26): Germany’s business outlook unexpectedly brightened for a sixth month in a row, underscoring the economy’s rebound from a prolonged downturn.

An expectations index by the Ifo institute rose to 91.6 in October from 90.4 the previous month. Economists surveyed by Bloomberg had anticipated a small decline to 90. A gauge measuring current conditions surprisingly edged down.

“The economics recovery is continuing,” Ifo president Clemens Fuest said on Monday in a statement. “Companies, however, assessed their current situation as slightly worse.”

Europe’s largest economy is enjoying a surprisingly strong year, despite inflation triggered by the Iran war and heat waves that crippled key waterways. Underpinning the expansion is vast spending on infrastructure, defence and artificial intelligence. The government recently upgraded its growth forecast for 2026 to 1.3%

The going has been bumpy. The Bundesbank estimates that output stagnated in the third quarter, when unseasonably hot weather lowered water levels in the Rhine river, disrupting a vital transport route for the country’s industrial sector.

Rising interest rates could create additional headwinds. European Central Bank officials have signalled that more tightening might be needed to tame price gains, though they’re widely expected to leave the key deposit rate at 2.5% on Thursday.

See also: EU plans to hit China with more import curbs in early 2027 — Bloomberg

But Germany’s central bank expects the final three months of the year to record “noticeable” growth, while business surveys from S&P Global last week pointed to a fourth straight month of expansion, despite momentum weakening.

title: EU plans to hit China with more import curbs in early 2027 — Bloomberg
article:
(Oct 26): The European Union is planning to use safeguard measures to cut imports of products from sectors including chemicals, furniture and machinery from China, according to people familiar with the matter.

The measures, which could take the form of either import caps or tariffs, may be presented as soon as the first quarter of 2027, said the people, who spoke on the condition of anonymity.

The European Commission is seeking to replicate its recent move to restrict the flow of hybrid vehicles into the EU, when it reached an agreement with Beijing to cap imports at 350,000 cars a year from China, according to the people. That level was deemed high enough to dissuade retaliation.

The latest action is part of a broad push by the EU to reduce its massive trade deficit with China, which reached €360 billion (US$404 billion or $516 billion) last year. The commission, which handles trade matters for the EU, is walking a fine line, trying to give its industry a boost without causing retaliation from Beijing and triggering a trade war.

Spokespeople from the commission didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment.

See also: UK house prices decline for a third month, official data show

“Our industries have called for action and we have heard them, and we will respond, including some more safeguards,” Commission President Ursula von der Leyen told reporters earlier this month.

Safeguard measures allow the EU to restrict products from a sector if there’s been a surge of imports into the bloc. The EU has already started to assess trade data to see where that’s the case, Bloomberg reported earlier.

The measures can take the form of import quotas, as in the case of the hybrid vehicles, or tariff-rate quotas, which apply a levy on imports above a certain volume to curb excess flows.

See also: Lane says greater global euro use may help ECB control inflation

The EU can choose to introduce the measures unilaterally without Beijing’s agreement. The people cautioned that the plans and the exact sectors the EU would target could change following discussions with member states and China.

China’s Commerce Ministry said in a statement earlier this month that the EU “cannot fantasise about gaining benefits by exerting pressure, nor should it underestimate” the country’s “determination and capability to protect its own interests”.

Just like the action set to be taken on hybrid cars and the bloc’s earlier move on steel, the new safeguard measures would comply with World Trade Organization rules and apply to other countries outside the European Economic Area, the people said.

Separately, the commission aims to put forward proposals in the coming weeks on implementing the hybrid vehicles cap so that it can enter into force in December, some of the people said. Those measures would apply for four years and China will see its quota rise by 6% a year after the first year of the cap. Quotas on vehicles from other countries such as Japan and South Korea would follow a similar logic, one of the people said.

Low-cost and at times subsidised goods from China have been flooding the continent, eroding domestic industries and putting local jobs at risk. That, coupled with falling demand and limited market access in China for many European goods, has led to a massive trade deficit of more than US$1 billion ($1.28 billion) a day — and rising.

EU leaders were united at a summit in Brussels earlier this month in urging the bloc’s executive to quickly take action across economic sectors and establish new powers to help cut the trade deficit and deter China from retaliating.

The commission is planning to present proposals before mid-December for a tool to diversify supplies as well as an instrument to rapidly react to any aggressive trade actions. A new instrument would do that by cutting access to the bloc’s single market for select goods and services in ways that are more agile and broader than current options allow, the people said.

It’s unclear whether Beijing is open to seeing its exports curbed much further beyond hybrid vehicles and it has responded strongly to the prospect of the EU introducing new tools.

The EU’s trade chief, Maros Sefcovic, is due to take stock of progress and discuss next steps with his Chinese counterparts early next year.

Agreements reached so far would also see Beijing cut tariffs on some auto parts, olive oil and ice cream. The EU is also seeking to improve market access in China and ease export procedures for critical minerals and permanent magnets.

title: China boosts self-driving push with VW, Xpeng technology trials
article:
(Oct 26): Volkswagen AG and Xpeng Inc secured approvals to trial autonomous driving systems on public roads in China, signalling a renewed push by authorities for larger-scale deployment following a safety review of the technology.

VW’s China unit said it’s started testing Level 3 technology in Hefei, with a target to deploy the system next year. Meanwhile, Xpeng said its robotaxi business received approval to carry out Level 4 testing across Guangzhou, with access initially offered through invitation codes before being expanded gradually.

The approvals add to signs that regulators have moved past a high-profile incident earlier this year involving Baidu Inc self-driving vehicles in Wuhan. The fallout saw China suspend new robotaxi licences in April and launch an industrywide safety review.

Bloomberg News reported in July that approvals had resumed, with Momenta Global Ltd receiving one of the first permits. But few other companies have publicly announced that they have received the green light to run trials.

The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, which oversees the sector, didn’t respond to a fax request for comment on the latest approvals.

See also: Tesla drops ‘self-driving’ branding to appease Europe regulators

China is trying to strike a balance between commercial expansion of the transformative auto technology and the risk to public safety. Regulators have already overhauled standards on door handles, advanced driver-assistance technology, batteries and lights.

title: Sembcorp gauges demand for US$394 mil India unit IPO — Bloomberg
article:
(Oct 26): Singapore-based Sembcorp Industries Ltd is meeting investors for a proposed initial public offering of its Indian unit, Sembcorp Green Infra Ltd, that could raise as much as US$394 million ($504 million), according to people familiar with the matter.

The Temasek Holdings Pte Ltd-backed renewable energy company is considering an IPO launch as early as December, the people said, asking not to be identified because the information is private.

Sembcorp Green Infra filed draft papers in August for an IPO comprising a fresh issue of shares worth as much as 37.5 billion rupees (US$394 million or $500 million) and is awaiting regulatory approval.

Deliberations are ongoing and details of the offering, including its timing and size, could change, the people said. Representatives for Sembcorp didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.

Sembcorp is working with Axis Capital Ltd, Citigroup Inc, CLSA, HSBC Holdings plc, ICICI Securities Ltd, IIFL Capital Services Ltd and Kotak Mahindra Capital Co, the people said.

India’s primary market is gathering momentum with the record IPO of Jio Platforms Ltd, which was subscribed more than 22 times last week. Several companies are preparing to tap the market over the next two months. IPOs in the country have raised nearly US$18 billion this year, putting the market on course to challenge last year’s record of about US$22.4 billion.

See also: Mi Material to be spun off from Bursa-listed parent; bets on China+1 for growth

Sembcorp Green Infra is among India’s 10 largest renewable independent power producers by operational capacity as of March 31, 2026, according to its IPO prospectus. The company has more than 75 renewable-energy assets across 18 states, with 7.6 gigawatts of gross renewable-energy capacity installed and under development in India.
